# Flyology CBOR

> Experimental streaming CBOR parser and transactional writer for Ada.

Flyology CBOR 0.1.0-dev is a local reviewed candidate. It is not available from a public GitHub repository or Alire index. The bounded parser and writer allocate no heap storage. Callers select every profile and syntax-depth bound explicitly. A Drain caller supplies event storage, and bounded writing callers select output capacity.

## Documentation

- [Overview](/): project boundary and design summary
- [Guide](/guide/): task-oriented entry points
- [Getting started](/guide/getting-started/): build and run maintained examples
- [Parsing](/guide/parsing/): Step, Drain, events, fragments, and lifecycle
- [Writing](/guide/writing/): bounded, allocating, and external transactional writers
- [Values and numbers](/guide/values-and-numbers/): raw CBOR values and checked conversion
- [Profiles and errors](/guide/profiles-and-errors/): explicit behavior identity and diagnostics
- [Architecture](/architecture/): storage, ownership, and publication boundaries
- [Support](/support/): current evidence and limitations
- [API reference](/api/): generated GNATdoc contracts

## Current boundary

- Parser events remain provisional until Document_Complete.
- Borrowed fragments refer only to the exact unchanged input from the producing call.
- Negative integers retain the raw CBOR argument for the mathematical value -1-n.
- Number helpers provide checked signed, unsigned, and Binary64 conversion.
- Floating values retain binary16, binary32, or binary64 width and exact bits.
- Tags remain syntax and carry no schema, Type IR, Reflection, or Wire identity.
- Ordinary Compact preserves caller order but is not canonical CBOR.
- The parser has no DOM or collector. The bounded core performs no allocation.
- Public repository creation, Alire publication, hosted CI, and downstream migration remain unauthorized.
